LanguageData.CC_Settings_ItemCardFirst_Tip: Opening the info for any item (the "i" button anywhere, a trade screen, a bill, a list, the inspect pane) opens Rimfolk's item card instead of the game's: food, a drink, a drug, medicine, a material (metal, wood, stone blocks, cloth, leather, wool, chunks, components, chemfuel and the like), a work of art held or placed, a book, a body part, a techprint, a neurotrainer or psytrainer, a genepack, xenogerm or embryo, something to use (a mech serum, a pulser, a mod's item), a shell, furniture in a crate, and anything else. It shows what the thing is good for in this colony, its tags, and by kind: who at home eats, takes, reads, learns from or could have it installed and why, what a material does to what is made of it, what a work of art or a piece of furniture does for its room, what a book teaches, a part's surgery and the faiths that care, a techprint's project, a xenogerm's genes, a use's risks, the guns that fire a shell; then the colony's stock, where it comes from, and how traders value it. Weapons and apparel keep their own cards; corpses keep the game's. Its button "All the game's stats" opens the game's card, and the game's card keeps its button back. Links followed inside the game's card stay in it. Off, the game's card opens as before, with a button to Rimfolk's card at its foot.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_ItemCardFirst: Every item opens as Rimfolk's item card; weapons and apparel keep theirs, and the game's card is one button away.
LanguageData.CC_ItemCard_NotCovered: Rimfolk's item card shows items; this (a weapon, apparel, a corpse, a creature or a building standing on the map) opens in its own card.
LanguageData.CC_ItemCard_GameCard_Tip: Open the game's own info card for this, with every stat it lists. Its button "Rimfolk's item card" brings you back here.
LanguageData.CC_ItemCard_OpenCard_Tip: Open Rimfolk's card for this: what it is good for in this colony, its tags, the colony's stock and what waits on it, where it comes from, and how traders value it.
